test_title: PYST 25: Selection Post (Graduate Level) - English Language (Held On 28 Jul, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
A sentence is provided in indirect speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding direct speech.

The supervisor asked whether the reports that were supposed to be finalized last week had been submitted to the review committee.

options.text: "Did you submit the reports meant to be finalized last week to the review committee?" the supervisor asked.
"Had the final reports from last week been submitted to the committee?" the supervisor asked.
"Have last week's reports been sent to the committee yet?" the supervisor asked.
"Were the reports due last week submitted to the review team?" the supervisor asked.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Direct Speech:** "Did you submit the reports meant to be finalized last week to the review committee?" the supervisor asked.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"whether... had been submitted" becomes "Did you submit"**
 
 
• The indirect question starts with "whether," which indicates a Yes/No question in direct speech.
 
• The Past Perfect tense in the indirect speech (**had been submitted**) correctly reverts to the Simple Past tense (**Did you submit**) in direct speech. While there is a shift from passive to active voice to make the direct quote sound more natural, it is the most accurate option provided.
 
 
 
• **"reports that were supposed to be finalized" becomes "reports meant to be finalized"**
 
 
• The phrase "meant to be" is a synonymous and accurate equivalent for "supposed to be" in this context, maintaining the original meaning regarding the missed deadline.
 
 
 
• **Reporting Verb:**
 
 
• The reporting verb "asked" remains the same and is placed at the end of the sentence in the direct form.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• The direct question is correctly enclosed in quotation marks.
 
• It begins with a capital letter and ends with a question mark inside the quotation marks.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"“Did you submit the reports meant to be finalized last week to the review committee?” the supervisor asked."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "Had the final reports from last week been submitted to the committee?"

 
 
• Changes the meaning by referring to them as "final reports" rather than reports that were "supposed to be finalized."
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "Have last week's reports been sent to the committee yet?"
 
 
• Changes the verb from "submitted" to "sent" and completely omits the critical clause about the reports being "supposed to be finalized."
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "Were the reports due last week submitted to the review team?"
 
 
• Incorrectly changes the entity from "review committee" to "review team," altering the specific nouns used in the original sentence.
